security_audit.summary: The skill intentionally contacts two publisher-controlled API endpoints and includes an opt-in Windows command that creates a recurring scheduled task. Most other static alerts are Markdown syntax or plain-text examples, but remote API content is processed without explicit validation or instruction-isolation safeguards.

remediation.issue: The documentation creates a persistent Windows scheduled task without showing consent checks, removal instructions, or a bounded lifetime.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before task creation, use least privilege, document the exact schedule, and provide a matching deletion command.

remediation.issue: Publisher-controlled API responses are passed into agent analysis and alerts without explicit schema validation or prompt-injection handling.
remediation.suggestion: Validate response schemas, treat all returned text as untrusted data, ignore embedded instructions, and escape content before message delivery.

remediation.issue: External requests rely on curl without documented timeouts, response limits, or redirect restrictions.
remediation.suggestion: Use fixed argument arrays, enforce HTTPS, disable unexpected redirects, and set connection timeouts and response-size limits.

content.user_title: Monitor Prediction Markets for Material Changes
content.value_statement: Prediction market changes can be difficult to track across frequent updates. This skill polls approved feeds and formats alerts for notable events and movements.
actual_capabilities: Fetches prediction news and active event data from two configured ME News API endpoints.
Identifies trending events, large trades, probability changes, and price deviations using documented thresholds.
Formats results as timestamped Markdown alerts with source links and risk notes.
Supports manual checks and optional recurring execution through external scheduling.
Can send alerts through an already configured OpenClaw message channel.
limitations: It depends on publisher-controlled API availability and data quality.
It does not execute trades or verify opportunities against primary market sources.
Scheduled checks and message delivery require external OpenClaw configuration.
Its alerts are informational and do not constitute financial advice.

use_cases.title: Review Current Market Activity
use_cases.description: Summarize active events and material probability changes before a research session.

use_cases.title: Detect Unusual Trading
use_cases.description: Highlight large trades and rapid market movements for manual investigation.

use_cases.title: Publish Scheduled Alerts
use_cases.description: Send formatted monitoring updates through an approved and preconfigured message channel.

prompt_templates.title: Check Popular Events
prompt_templates.prompt: Check the approved prediction-market feeds and list the current popular events with probabilities and source links.

prompt_templates.title: Find Large Trades
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the latest feed data for trades above $100,000. Include event, direction, amount, probability impact, and source.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze Probability Moves
prompt_templates.prompt: Identify events with at least a 10 percent hourly move or 20 percent daily move. Explain available evidence and data limitations.

prompt_templates.title: Assess Potential Opportunities
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare current probabilities with available historical values. Rank deviations, explain assumptions, cite sources, and include risk notes without presenting financial advice.

output_examples.output: Popular event update: Event A is at 62 percent with elevated volume. Review the linked market source before making decisions.

output_examples.input: Find large trades from the latest feed.
output_examples.output: Large trade alert: A $250,000 Yes trade moved the event probability from 38 to 42 percent. Source validation is recommended.
Probability alert: Event B rose 13 percentage points in one hour while volume reached 5.2 times its daily average.

best_practices: Validate important alerts against primary market sources before acting.
Start with manual checks before enabling recurring jobs or message delivery.
Use conservative polling intervals and review API rate limits.
anti_patterns: Do not treat generated opportunity labels as financial advice.
Do not enable scheduled jobs without explicit approval and removal instructions.
Do not forward unvalidated remote text into privileged agent instructions.

faq.question: Which data sources does this skill use?
faq.answer: It uses two configured ME News endpoints for prediction news and active event data.

faq.question: Does this skill place trades?
faq.answer: No. It analyzes feed data and produces informational alerts only.

faq.question: Can it send notifications?
faq.answer: Yes, but only through an OpenClaw message channel that the user configured separately.

faq.question: Does monitoring start automatically?
faq.answer: No scheduler is bundled. Recurring checks require a user-configured cron job or Windows scheduled task.

faq.question: Are the opportunity alerts financial advice?
faq.answer: No. Users should review source data, market rules, liquidity, and personal risk before making decisions.

faq.question: What happens when an API request fails?
faq.answer: The instructions allow web_fetch as a fallback and require reporting the HTTP status and a short error summary.
